I wrote a blackjack game, mock vending machine, simple IM client, and basic web browser (download html but not interpret it) as my starting projects.

When buying unleaded, the price is the same for cash or credit. Why is diesel different?
Why do gas stations charge more for diesel when using a credit card?

The credit card fees on a hundred gallon fill-up of diesel costs the station 10x more than the ten gallons you put in your econobox. Why hire employees to deal with ten customers coming in for a discount when you can get the same financial result from one truck driver?
Thanks, that makes sense. You would think truckers would just pay cash but I'm guessing they're getting credit card rewards and still come out ahead.
Cash is legal tender. Credit cards are a convenience offered by the merchant, and that convenience (yours, not theirs) costs them money.
